title: Derived scalar localization is reflective with its normalized unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $s$ a global section. Put $S=R[1/s]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories and localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write $E(M)=S\otimes_R M$ and $U_0$ for ordinary extension and restriction. Let $F=S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U$ be derived restriction, with the evaluation-normalized adjunction $F\dashv U$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$. Then $E,U_0$ are exact, and there are natural identifications $F(Q_RM)\cong Q_S(E M)$ and $U(Q_SN)\cong Q_R(U_0N)$ for every complex $M$ over $R$ and $N$ over $S$. In these identifications $\eta_{Q_RM}$ is represented by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and $\varepsilon_{Q_SN}$ by multiplication $S\otimes_R U_0N\to N$, $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$. The counit is an isomorphism for every $N\in D(S)$. For every $A\in D(R)$ and $N\in D(S)$, precomposition with $\eta_A$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(UFA,UN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(A,UN),\qquad q\longmapsto q\circ\eta_A,$$
with inverse $h\longmapsto U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(h)$. In particular $UF(\eta_A)=\eta_{UFA}$. No boundedness or nonzero hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-sheaf-exact]. The prescribed object and map equalities identify its exact extension functor naturally with the ordinary functor m.E of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so exactness transfers to m.E. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] to this presentation. Evaluating its Hom formula on the identity of the extension gives the unit formula. The inverse image of the identity under its Hom equivalence is the counit. Its value on 1 tensor x is x; linearity of the tensor sheafification unit and of the counit gives its value b times x on every pure tensor.

Use the exact termwise factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and the universal-comparison assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. Applied to the universal pair m.T,m.ε of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], this makes m.ε invertible on every complex. Set c=asIso(m.ε). The two comparison isomorphisms c and the restriction factorization define commuting squares with localization. Localize the termwise ordinary adjunction, using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (Mathlib Adjunction.localization). Its explicit localization_unit_app and localization_counit_app formulas, followed by cancellation of comparison isomorphisms, are exactly the two required normalization equations. This directly constructs the normalized adjunction for the specified m.T; no choice of a second derived extension or comparison on K-flat representatives is required.

Prove ordinary restriction fully faithful. Write B(V)=R(V)[1/s(V)] and α:B→S for ring sheafification [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Its moduleComparison identifies the underlying map of α, followed by an isomorphism, with the module sheafification unit. The unit is locally surjective by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]; cancellation of the isomorphism proves α locally surjective. Given an R-linear sheaf map g between restrictions of S-module sheaves, prove it B-linear sectionwise: express b in B(V) by b times d=a, where d is a power of s. After α, multiplication by d is invertible. Multiply the desired equality g(α(b)x)=α(b)g(x) by α(d), use R-linearity twice and α(b)α(d)=α(a), then cancel. The locally surjective scalar-change Hom equivalence for α extends this B-linear map to an S-linear map with the identical underlying additive map. This proves fullness, while faithfulness follows from unchanged underlying maps. The ordinary adjunction counit is therefore invertible. This argument uses local surjectivity of α, never surjectivity on sections.

The termwise counit is an isomorphism: its components are the ordinary counit isomorphisms just established. The derived counit formula therefore makes the derived counit invertible on every localized complex. For any object N choose a representative and an isomorphism Q(K)→N by [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive]. Naturality expresses the counit at N as the composite of that isomorphism, the counit at Q(K), and the image of its inverse. Hence it is invertible everywhere.

Cancel U(ε_FA) in the two triangle identities to obtain UF(η_A)=η_UFA. Define the Hom equivalence by q↦η_A followed by q, with inverse h↦UF(h) followed by U(ε_N). For one inverse equation use naturality of η at h followed by the right triangle identity. For the other expand UF(q after η_A), substitute the unit identity, use naturality at q, and apply the same right triangle identity. All arguments work for unbounded complexes and for zero or nilpotent s.

This correctly avoids assuming S(V)=R(V)[1/s]. Step 6: invertibility extends to all of D(S) by conjugation. Steps 7–8: the triangle-identity and naturality algebra is verified, and it gives exactly the displayed inverse. Edge cases: s a unit, s zero or nilpotent (S=0), unbounded complexes.
